samples.summary: PATCH /documents/:id answers 200 for a request that wrote nothing when the body names only unrecognized fields
samples.evidence: `update` builds `data` field-by-field (`title`, `folderId`) and then unconditionally calls `updateDocument({ where, data })`. The body is an inline type, not a DTO class, so the global `ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true })` (packages/backend/src/main.ts:66) does not apply and cannot 400 on unknown keys. A caller sending e.g. `{ workspaceId: 'ws-2' }` (a move the sibling web route at document.controller.ts:332 does support) or a misspelled `{ folder_id: 'f-1' }` now gets `data = {}`, `documentService.updateDocument` skips even the `updatedAt` bump (document.service.ts:99), and the response is a 200 with the unchanged row — indistinguishable from a successful update. The change's own spec asserts this behaviour ('writes nothing when the body carries only unknown fields'), so it is deliberate, but a write API that reports success for a request it ignored will silently strand any client that asks for a field this handler does not know.

samples.summary: `folders delete` help text omits that descendant folders are deleted, contradicting the schema registry entry for the same command
samples.evidence: The CLI description is 'Delete a folder; its documents return to the workspace root (never deleted)'. It says nothing about subfolders, yet `Folder.parent` is `onDelete: Cascade` (prisma/schema.prisma:137) and the schema registry entry added in this same diff says 'Delete a folder and its descendant folders' (packages/cli/src/schema/registry.ts, folders.delete). For a `destructive` command whose only interactive safety net is its help text, the reassuring 'never deleted' phrasing understates what the call actually destroys.

samples.summary: New commands validate `--format` only after the `--dry-run` branch, so `--dry-run --format bogus` prints a preview instead of erroring — inconsistent with `folders list`/`create` in the same file
samples.evidence: `folders rename` (line ~86), `folders move`, `folders delete`, and `docs copy` / `docs move` (packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:182, 204) call `printDryRun(...)` and `return` before `parseOutputFormat(opts.format)`. `folders list` (line ~57) and `folders create` (line ~78) parse the format first, so an invalid `--format` under `--dry-run` errors there and is silently accepted here. `--dry-run` is documented elsewhere in this CLI as validating inputs (docs.ts:82-84).

samples.summary: Presenting a workspace-matching API key whose minter has left now yields 403 even when a valid share token is supplied, where sending no credential at all would succeed
samples.evidence: The API-key branch of `assertCanRead` returns or throws before reaching the `if (token)` fallback at line 128, so an integration that sends both `Authorization: Bearer wfb_...` and `?token=` is refused, while the identical anonymous request with the token alone is served. The JWT branch deliberately falls through in exactly this situation (lines 114-127, 'A logged-in non-member may still hold a share token'). The added spec asserts the key behaviour as intended, so this is a deliberate asymmetry, but it makes supplying a credential strictly worse than omitting it and will read as a broken image to a caller that always attaches its key.

samples.summary: The guard resolves the workspace id and then calls `assertMember`, which resolves it a second time on every v1 request
samples.evidence: Line 37 does `const resolvedId = await this.workspaceService.resolveId(workspaceId)` and line 44 passes that uuid to `assertMember`, whose first statement is `const resolvedId = await this.resolveId(workspaceId)` (workspace.service.ts:237). For a uuid `resolveId` short-circuits without a query, so this is free in the common case, but the same duplication now also runs for every API-key request (previously the key path returned at line 43 before any membership lookup), adding a membership query per request on the whole v1 surface.
